newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom faces tough ally choice.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom faces tough ally choice.

text.p: Portugal Telecom may be leaning towards Concert, the Anglo-U.S. telecoms venture, as its international strategic partner, but the choice facing the Portuguese is not easy, analysts say.

The calculation is made particularly complex by uncertainty over the future alignment of Spain's Telefonica, a key concern to the Portuguese given their geographic proximity and similar involvement in Latin America's growing market.

"It looks as if Concert is the front runner," said telecommunications analyst James Golob of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, referring to the venture between British Telecom and the U.S. MCI Communications Corp.
"But Telefonica is an important issue. I would not necessarily say that it is cut and dried. It is a complicated decision," he added.

The state-controlled Portuguese concern said it would announce its decision about alliances in the first half of April. A spokeswoman denied a local newspaper report that the company's board would take the plunge at a meeting on Thursday.

In addition to Concert, the Global One partnership between Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and U.S. Sprint, and Unisource, which includes AT&T, Dutch, Swedish and Swiss groups, are wooing the Portuguese.
While Portugal is only a small market, Portugal Telecom offers a gateway into Latin America through its historical connections and its alliance with Brazil's Telebras.
"Portugal is a second tier market but if you want business there, there is no alternative. Its alliance with Telebras is also a draw," said Golob.
The company has regularly put the damper on local press reports claiming a link with Concert has been agreed. It says that talks with all three groups are continuing.
Analysts say Concert's advantage is that it is generally seen -- at the moment -- to be the industry leader in Europe.

A disadvantage, particularly for a small player like Portugal Telecom, is that Concert is also regarded as fairly autocratic, with the main movers dictating strategies that the others are expected to follow.
Concert could also be said to offer potentially less protection against predatory threats to the local Portuguese market than its rivals.
Of the two potential threats, France Telecom is inside Global One, while Telefonica is part of Unisource.

But whether Telefonica remains there for long is an open question. The Spanish operator is searching for a U.S. ally for its international subsidiary TISA. Should it opt for anyone other than AT&T, analysts feel it would be signalling its withdrawal from Uniscource, which is struggling to achieve any real degree of integration in Europe. MCI is a potential partner for TISA.
